facts.title: Abraham Lincoln — Civil War president
facts.text: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States and president during the Civil War; this is retained as historic source-attributed context.

facts.title: Theodore Roosevelt — Nobel Peace Prize
facts.text: Theodore Roosevelt, the 26th U.S. president, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1906.

facts.title: Woodrow Wilson — Nobel Peace Prize
facts.text: Woodrow Wilson, the 28th U.S. president, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1919.

facts.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt — presidency
facts.text: Franklin D. Roosevelt served as U.S. president from 1933 to 1945; this historic office record is retained with source attribution.

facts.title: Jimmy Carter — Nobel Peace Prize
facts.text: Jimmy Carter, the 39th U.S. president, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002.

facts.title: John F. Kennedy — historic office
facts.text: John F. Kennedy was the 35th U.S. president and was assassinated in 1963; this is bounded historic biographical context.

facts.title: Richard Nixon — resignation
facts.text: Richard Nixon was the 37th U.S. president and resigned in 1974; the record is retained as historic source-attributed context.

facts.title: Barack Obama — Nobel Peace Prize
facts.text: Barack Obama, the 44th U.S. president, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009.

facts.title: Assassinated U.S. presidents — source chronology
facts.text: The source lists Abraham Lincoln (1865), James A. Garfield (1881), William McKinley (1901), and John F. Kennedy (1963) as U.S. presidents killed by assassins; retained as historic source-attributed chronology.

facts.title: U.S. presidential impeachment — historic dates
facts.text: The House of Representatives impeached Andrew Johnson in 1868, Bill Clinton in 1998, and Donald Trump in 2019 and 2021.

facts.title: September 11 attacks — historical event
facts.text: The September 11, 2001 attacks included impacts at the World Trade Center in New York and the Pentagon; this record is bounded historic context.

facts.title: U.S. landmarks — source reference
facts.text: The source identifies Independence Hall, the Pentagon, Golden Gate, Cape Kennedy, and Hollywood/Los Angeles as notable U.S. places; retained as source-attributed geography.

notes.title: Presidential-reference boundary
notes.text: Historic office and Nobel records are retained; rankings, unattributed quotations, and superlatives are excluded.

notes.title: Presidential policy boundary
notes.text: Historic office chronology is retained. Military, conflict, and ideological descriptions are excluded or retained only through explicit historic scope.

notes.title: Security and conflict boundary
notes.text: The source’s War on Terror, Afghanistan, Iraq, Grenada, and doctrine claims are withheld rather than rendered as unqualified learning facts.

notes.title: Current-office boundary
notes.text: Current office, campaign slogan, party-ideology, and detention claims are excluded. Historic prize and assassination records are retained with scope.

notes.title: Impeachment and 9/11 boundary
notes.text: Impeachment and 9/11 records are retained only as historically bounded, externally corroborated material. Diplomatic and security-policy claims are excluded.
